title: ai_semantic_cache plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `ai_semantic_cache` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component AiSemanticCacheConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

AiSemanticCacheConfig.description: Plugin: ai_semantic_cache — Caches LLM responses keyed by family-correct prompts across Ferrum's recognized request families (OpenAI Chat messages, Anthropic messages/system, OpenAI Responses input/instructions, Gemini/Vertex contents/systemInstruction, Cohere chat_history/message, legacy prompt, TGI inputs, and Titan inputText). Unknown or ambiguous JSON shapes bypass caching. Exact keys preserve LLM-significant prompt case and whitespace while applying structurally safe canonicalization; optional semantic similarity uses a configured embedding provider and a local HNSW vector index. Both exact and semantic scope keys bind the shared canonical effective-destination partition (proxy namespace and ID, listen path, upstream or direct host/port/scheme, route authority, rewritten path), a mandatory caller-authorization partition, and a length-framed backend-visible request-context digest (original client authority and Host, method, path, the effective outbound query, and every non-credential request header; credential header values are digested, never embedded). Only transport/hop-by-hop framing fields Ferrum provably regenerates for the backend hop are excluded from that binding (Host/authority is bound separately); tracing and correlation headers such as traceparent, tracestate, b3, X-B3-*, X-Request-Id and X-Correlation-Id ARE bound, because a client-supplied value can be preserved and reaches the origin. The one exception is a correlation_id header whose live value private request provenance records as generated by the gateway on this request (the rule response_caching applies), plus the x-ratelimit-* values the owning rate_limiting instance staged; both change on every request. A conservative miss is preferred over an unbound dimension. Lookup runs at priority 4057 in the final-request-body hook, not before_proxy, so the partition and the prompt digest describe the fully transformed request the provider would receive; it runs after ai_prompt_compressor (4055) enforces its staged marker-sanitization rejection and before ai_federation (4060) performs provider I/O, while every before_proxy admission guardrail still precedes any hit. Supports local DashMap and Redis exact-response storage. Redis mode requires redis_integrity_key and treats Redis as an untrusted, authenticated trust boundary. Quarantine DEL failures are counted with rate-limited warnings (no keys/payloads/credentials) and suppressed by a bounded per-instance local fingerprint+TTL marker (fingerprints only after admission failure; constant-work capacity eviction) so the same poisoned remote value cannot amplify download/parse/delete on every request; suppression never converts a miss into a hit. Multiple instances on one proxy namespace request staging metadata under ai_semantic_cache.<instance_id>.* and keep embedding/scope vectors in per-instance RequestContext maps so differing key policies and semantic/non-semantic combinations remain independent across priority order and reload generations. Unknown root, semantic-policy, and Redis sync keys are rejected at admission with path-qualified diagnostics (registration policy KeepLastKnownGood). There are no intentionally open maps. All numeric retention/time bounds must be positive. The constructor additionally enforces max_entry_size_bytes <= max_total_size_bytes (including omitted defaults), the 32 UTF-8 byte redis_integrity_key minimum, platform-sized integer limits, URL parsing, and the deployment backend egress policy. These residual checks are not fully expressible in this schema. Provider-managed Responses conversations, Gemini retained contexts, and Cohere conversation_id requests bypass replay; other unmodeled root context is canonically bound to exact and semantic identities. Request bodies with duplicate JSON members, a request Cache-Control no-store/no-cache, or an unprovable response-presentation policy also bypass. Instruction state (system, developer, instructions, systemInstruction, preamble, Cohere SYSTEM history) is bound byte-exactly in semantic scopes. Exact keys and semantic scopes bind the request's response-policy provenance (RTDS gate content and static presentation-policy digest). Responses with Cache-Control no-store/private or Set-Cookie are not stored; provider-backed ai_federation answers are. Cache hits preserve finalized application bodies while current response enforcement, live header rules, and negotiated compression still run.

ttl_seconds.description: Time-to-live for cached entries in seconds

max_entries.description: Maximum number of cached entries (local mode). In semantic mode, HNSW snapshot memory scales with this count and is charged against max_total_size_bytes.

max_entry_size_bytes.description: Maximum size of a single cached response body in bytes (1 MiB). Hard maximum 16 MiB; larger values are rejected at admission so Redis transfer caps cannot saturate platform integers.

max_total_size_bytes.description: Maximum retained local cache memory in bytes (100 MiB, local mode; hard maximum 1 GiB). Includes response bodies, cached headers, semantic scope keys, retained embedding vectors, published HNSW snapshot generations, and in-flight rebuild workspace reservations. Concurrent stores and rebuilds use lock-free byte leases so overlapping old/candidate generations are charged at peak and failed/superseded rebuilds release promptly. A store or rebuild that cannot reserve is skipped.

include_model_in_key.description: Include the model name in the cache key (different models get separate cache entries)

include_params_in_key.description: Include request parameters (temperature, top_p, max_tokens) in the cache key. Default `true` — different sampling params produce different responses and must not collide. Set `false` only when cross-parameter cache reuse is intentional.

scope_by_consumer.description: Additionally include the authenticated consumer's display identity in the cache key. Caller isolation no longer depends on this flag — every exact and semantic key binds a mandatory caller-authorization partition (authentication mechanism, resolved identity/consumer, peer SPIFFE identity, and SHA-256 digests of every credential header presented), so two credentials resolving to one display subject with different scopes can never share a retained completion. Setting `false` no longer lets distinct callers share entries.

anonymous_caller_scope.description: How anonymous callers (no gateway identity, no credential header, no peer SPIFFE identity) are partitioned. caller_address (default) binds the gateway-resolved canonical peer address, which the origin observes through Ferrum's regenerated X-Forwarded-For; a request whose canonical address cannot be parsed is refused rather than keyed incompletely. shared is an explicit operator attestation that the origin does not vary its result by caller address on this route — only set it when that is known-safe, because it re-opens cross-caller replay for address-sensitive origins. It applies to anonymous callers only: an authenticated caller always binds its canonical peer address, because the backend receives Ferrum's regenerated forwarding identity for that caller too and may vary policy or content by it.

cache_multimodal.description: Multimodal request caching mode for non-text content parts. `reject` bypasses cache lookup/store, `exact_only` uses hashed fingerprints for exact matches and disables semantic hits, and `include_fingerprints` also includes those fingerprints in semantic scope keys. The parser and schema accept surrounding whitespace, ASCII case variants, and the listed underscore/hyphen aliases.

semantic_similarity_enabled.description: Enable embedding-based semantic lookup after exact Redis/local misses. Exact matching remains active when this is disabled or enabled.

semantic_embedding_provider.description: Embedding provider request/response format. Values are trimmed and ASCII case-insensitive. Aliases include openai_compatible/openai-compatible, azure/azure-openai, voyageai/voyage_ai/anthropic/claude, google/gemini/google-gemini, vertex/vertex_ai/vertex-ai/google-vertex, amazon_titan/amazon-titan/bedrock-titan, and cohere_bedrock/cohere-bedrock/bedrock-cohere; anthropic and claude are aliases for Voyage-compatible embeddings because Claude does not expose a native embedding model.

semantic_embedding_endpoint.description: Nonblank embedding endpoint. Required and validated as an HTTP(S) URL when semantic_similarity_enabled is true; disabled semantic mode only checks that the supplied string is nonblank. A cleartext http:// URL is admitted only to a loopback IP literal written as a dotted-quad 127.d.d.d or [::1] (other spellings and the name localhost do not qualify) unless semantic_embedding_allow_plaintext is true. Must not include URL userinfo; use semantic_embedding_api_key for credentials. Query parameters and path tokens required by signed or credential-bearing endpoints are preserved on the outbound request but stripped from logs and error diagnostics (canonical redacted form uses scheme/host/port plus /...). OpenAI-compatible endpoints use input/model JSON; other providers send native embedding JSON.

semantic_embedding_model.description: Model name sent in the embedding request body. Omit for local endpoints that do not require a model field.

semantic_embedding_input_type.description: Provider-specific input or task type, such as query/document for Voyage, search_query/search_document for Cohere, SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY for Gemini, or Vertex task_type.

semantic_embedding_output_dimension.description: Provider-specific reduced embedding dimension from 1 to 16384 when supported. Mistral uses output_dimension; OpenAI and Azure OpenAI use dimensions.

semantic_embedding_api_key.description: Nonblank API key; the final header value is validated at admission and retained as sensitive. Invalid header characters in the key or scheme are rejected without echoing values. Sent in semantic_embedding_auth_header with semantic_embedding_auth_scheme when configured.

semantic_embedding_auth_header.description: HTTP header used for semantic_embedding_api_key. Defaults to Authorization, except Azure OpenAI uses api-key and Google Gemini uses x-goog-api-key. Must not be the gateway-owned X-Ferrum-Hops proxy hop count (any case, `_` or `-`), which the embedding call carries itself.

semantic_embedding_allow_plaintext.description: Admit a cleartext http:// semantic_embedding_endpoint whose host is not a loopback IP literal. The embedding API key then crosses the network in clear.

semantic_embedding_auth_scheme.description: Prefix for the API key header value. Defaults to Bearer, except Azure OpenAI and Google Gemini send the raw key. Set to an empty string to send the raw key.

semantic_similarity_threshold.description: Minimum cosine similarity for a semantic cache hit.

semantic_vector_max_candidates.description: Number of nearest HNSW candidates to inspect during semantic lookup (`ef_search` / `ef_construction`). Hard maximum 1024; larger values are rejected at admission so semantic search cannot be configured into an unbounded graph walk.

semantic_embedding_timeout_ms.description: Per-request timeout for embedding calls in milliseconds. Embedding failures fall back to a normal exact-cache miss.

sync_mode.description: Storage backend: local or redis, ASCII case-insensitive without whitespace trimming. Redis requires redis_url and redis_integrity_key.

redis_url.description: Redis connection URL (required when sync_mode is redis). Must not carry a URL fragment. The database path selects an integer from 0 to 2147483647, without a sign, zero-padding, or extra slashes. An absent path or bare slash selects database 0. URL port validity and server database availability remain constructor/server checks. TLS skip-verify is only FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY. URL-embedded userinfo is accepted but never disclosed: connection/health-check logs and non-admin/audit projections keep only the scheme, host, port, and database, replace the userinfo, and replace query/fragment data with `[REDACTED_QUERY]` and `[REDACTED_FRAGMENT]` markers. Full admin reads stay raw.

redis_key_prefix.description: Redis key namespace prefix. When omitted, the runtime derives `{FERRUM_NAMESPACE}:ai_cache` (for example `ferrum:ai_cache` when the namespace is `ferrum`). No static OpenAPI default is advertised because the value depends on the gateway namespace.

redis_pool_size.description: Number of multiplexed Redis connections. Must be between 1 and 128.

redis_health_check_interval_seconds.description: Interval for background health check pings when Redis is unavailable

redis_integrity_key.description: Narrowly scoped HMAC-SHA256 secret that authenticates Redis cache envelopes. Required when sync_mode is redis (fail closed if omitted). Minimum 32 UTF-8 bytes, checked by the constructor (JSON Schema string length counts characters). Bound to the full status/header/body envelope and the Redis namespace/key context. Compared in constant time; never logged, and replaced by [REDACTED] in admin audit diffs and in viewer/operator plugin-config reads (full admin reads stay raw so rotation by read-modify-write works). Rolling the key quarantines prior entries — there is no legacy unauthenticated read path during build-out.
